# 1. Introduction to R

R is a programming language and software environment used for statistical computing, data analysis, and data visualization.
```{r calculator}
# Basic calculations
20 + 10
50 - 8
30 * 20
90 / 3
6^4
```

# 2. Data structures in R

## 2.1 Vectors

A vector stores values of the same basic type.

```{r vectors}
# Numeric vector
study_hours <- c(2.5, 3, 4, 1.5, 5)
summary(study_hours)

# Calculate the average study time
mean(study_hours)

# Logical vector
passed <- c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)

# Character vector
students <- c("Fiston", "Aloys", "Ange", "Mwizerwa")

# Integer vector
days <- 1:7

# Complex vector
complex_values <- c(4 + 2i, 3 + 2i)

# Check the type of a vector
class(complex_values)
```

## 2.2 Matrices

A matrix stores data in rows and columns. All its values should have the same basic type.

```{r matrices}
# Create a matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns

x <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2, ncol = 3)
x

# Create another matrix

y <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 6, ncol = 4)
y

# Multiply the two matrices
x %*% y
```

## 2.3 Lists

A list can store different types of values together.

```{r lists}
# Create a list with different types of information
student_info <- list(
  name = "Fiston",
  age = 25,
  registered = TRUE,
  score = 80 + 2i
)

student_info

# Access the student's name
student_info[[1]]
```

## 2.4 Factors

A factor is used to represent categories.

```{r factors}
# Record whether students completed an assignment
assignment_status <- factor(
  c("Completed", "Completed", "Not completed", "Completed", "Not completed")
)

assignment_status
levels(assignment_status)
```

## 2.5 Missing values

R uses `NA` to represent missing information.

```{r missing-values}
# Create a vector with one missing value
scores <- c(60, 84, NA, 85, 78)

# Identify the missing value
is.na(scores)

# Remove missing values when calculating the average
mean(scores, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r complete-cases}
# Check which rows have complete information
height <- c(160, 155, NA, 140, 185)
weight <- c(68, 58, 70, NA, 70)

complete.cases(height, weight)
```

## 2.6 Coercion

R converts values to a common type when different types are combined in one vector.

```{r coercion}
# Numbers become characters when text is included
mixed_values <- c(40, 30, "Ten")
mixed_values

# TRUE is counted as 1 and FALSE as 0
sum(c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE))
```

```{r}
performance1 <- data.frame(
  Subject = names(numeric_data),

)
```

```{r}

# Create a new dataset from the original student data
performance2 <- performance

# Identify the subject columns
subjects <- c(
  "Mathematics",
  "English",
  "Biology",
  "Computer_Studies"
)

# Calculate each student's average mark
performance2$Total_Average <- rowMeans(
  performance2[, subjects, drop = FALSE],
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# Assign Pass or Fail
performance2$Decision <- ifelse(
  performance2$Total_Average >= 60,
  "Pass",
  "Fail"
)

# Display the new dataset
head(performance2, 10)

# Count pass and fail
table(performance2$Decision)

```

# Two categorical variables

```{r}
ucba <- data.frame(UCBAdmissions)
head(ucba)
(cross <- xtabs(Freq ~ Gender + Admit, data = ucba))

# Is there gender bias in UCB graduate admission?

```

## Simpson's paradox

A trend in the combined data disappears or reverses when the data are split into groups.

```{r}
cross2 <- xtabs(Freq ~ Gender + Admit, data = ucba[ucba$Dept == "F", ])
prop.table(cross2, 1)
```

# Subsetting: `$`, `[]`, `[[]]`

Leadership data: how do men and women differ in the way they lead?
Answers: 1 = strongly disagree ... 5 = strongly agree. In `age`, 99 means missing.

```{r}
manager <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
country <- c("US", "US", "UK", "UK", "UK")
gender  <- c("M", "F", "F", "M", "F")
age     <- c(32, 45, 25, 39, 99)
q1 <- c(5, 3, 3, 3, 2)
q2 <- c(4, 5, 5, 3, 2)
q3 <- c(5, 2, 5, 4, 1)
q4 <- c(5, 5, 5, NA, 2)
q5 <- c(5, 5, 2, NA, 1)

leadership <- data.frame(manager, country, gender, age, q1, q2, q3, q4, q5)
str(leadership)
names(leadership)
```

## Missing values and age categories

```{r}
leadership$age[leadership$age == 99] <- NA
# View(leadership)

leadership$agecat[leadership$age > 75] <- "Elder"
leadership$agecat[leadership$age >= 35 & leadership$age <= 75] <- "Middle Aged"
leadership$agecat[leadership$age < 35] <- "Young"
leadership
```

## Handling missing values: listwise deletion

```{r}
is.na(leadership[, 5:9])
newdata <- na.omit(leadership)
newdata
```

## Sorting

```{r}
order(leadership$age)
newdata2 <- leadership[order(leadership$age), ]
newdata2
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Horizontally (by a common key):

# rbind(dataframeA, dataframeB)
```

```{r}
leadership[[4]]

newdata6 <- leadership[c(2, 4, 5), ]

newdata7

# Men older than 30
(newdata7 <- leadership[leadership$gender == "M" & leadership$age > 30, ])
```

# Dataset

30 rows, with a few `NA` values for practice.

```{r data}
install.packages("tibble")
library(tibble)

# Create a students dataset
students <- tibble(
  id = 1:30,

  name = c("Emmanuel", "Patrick", "Diane", "Eric", "Claudine",
           "Samuel", "Alice", "David", "Chantal", "Kevin",
           "Jean", "Olive", "Sandrine", "Felix", "Esther",
           "Claude", "Aline", "Joseph", "Grace", "Daniel",
           "Beatha", "Benjamin", "Ange", "Christian", "Solange",
           "Fabrice", "Mireille", "Alexis", "Florence", "Theogene"),

  district = rep(c("Gasabo", "Kicukiro", "Nyarugenge",
                   "Huye", "Musanze", "Rubavu"), times = 5),

  grade = rep(c("S1", "S2", "S3"), each = 10),

  math = c(78, 65, 88, 54, 92, 71, 60, 85, NA, 95,
           67, 73, 58, 81, 90, 62, 77, 69, 84, 55,
           72, 64, 93, NA, 86, 79, 68, 91, 59, 75),

  english = c(70, 72, 80, 60, 85, 66, 58, 78, 55, 90,
              64, 70, 62, 75, 88, 59, 73, NA, 80, 61,
              69, 60, 87, 52, 79, 74, 71, 84, 63, 77),

  kinyarwanda = c(82, 75, 90, 68, 88, 79, 72, 91, 66, 94,
                  77, 80, 70, 85, 92, 74, 81, 76, 89, 69,
                  78, 73, 95, 64, 87, 83, 75, 90, 71, 84),

  tuition = rep(c(50000, 75000, 100000), times = 10),

  date = seq(as.Date("2026-01-12"),
             by = "week",
             length.out = 30)
)

# Display the students dataset
View(students)




```


## Inspect the dataset

```{r inspect}
glimpse(students)
head(students)
summary(students)
colSums(is.na(students))   # NAs per column
```

# dplyr: data manipulation

## filter(): choose rows

```{r filter}
students %>% filter(math >= 80)
students %>% filter(district == "Gasabo", grade == "S1")
students %>% filter(district %in% c("Huye", "Musanze"))
students %>% filter(between(math, 60, 80))
students %>% filter(is.na(math))
```

## select(): choose columns

```{r select}
students %>% select(name, district, math)
students %>% select(name, math:kinyarwanda)
students %>% select(-id, -date)
students %>% select(starts_with("e"))
students %>% select(where(is.numeric))
```

## arrange(): sort

```{r arrange}
students %>% arrange(math)
students %>% arrange(desc(kinyarwanda))
students %>% arrange(district, desc(math))
```

## mutate(): create new columns

```{r mutate}
students <- students %>%
  mutate(
    average = rowMeans(across(math:kinyarwanda), na.rm = TRUE),
    level = case_when(
      average >= 85 ~ "Excellent",
      average >= 70 ~ "Good",
      average >= 60 ~ "Average",
      TRUE          ~ "Low"
    ),
    passed = if_else(average >= 60, "Yes", "No"),
    name_upper = str_to_upper(name)
  )

students
```

## rename() and relocate()

```{r rename}
students %>% rename(class = grade)
students %>% relocate(average, .after = name)
```

## count(), distinct(), n_distinct()

```{r count}
students %>% count(district)
students %>% count(grade, sex)
students %>% count(level, sort = TRUE)
students %>% distinct(district)
n_distinct(students$district)
```

## group_by() + summarise(): aggregate

```{r summarise}
students %>%
  group_by(district) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    math_avg = mean(math, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_kinyarwanda = max(kinyarwanda),
    median_avg = median(average)
  )

students %>%
  group_by(grade, sex) %>%
  summarise(average = mean(average), .groups = "drop")
```

## across(): apply one function to many columns

```{r across}
students %>%
  summarise(across(math:kinyarwanda, ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

## slice_*(): pick specific rows

```{r slice}
students %>% slice_max(average, n = 5)
students %>% slice_min(average, n = 5)
students %>% slice_head(n = 3)
students %>% slice_sample(n = 3)
students %>% group_by(district) %>% slice_max(average, n = 1)
```

## Window functions: rank, lag, cumsum

```{r window}
students %>%
  mutate(rank = min_rank(desc(average)),
         change = average - lag(average),
         running_total = cumsum(tuition)) %>%
  select(name, average, rank, change, running_total)
```

## pull(): extract a column as a vector

```{r pull}
students %>% pull(math) %>% mean(na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Joins: combine two tables

```{r joins}
provinces <- tibble(
  district = c("Gasabo", "Kicukiro", "Nyarugenge", "Huye", "Musanze", "Rubavu"),
  province = c("Kigali", "Kigali", "Kigali", "South", "North", "West")
)

students %>% left_join(provinces, by = "district")
students %>% inner_join(provinces, by = "district")
provinces %>% anti_join(students %>% filter(district == "Huye"), by = "district")
```

## bind_rows()

```{r bind}
new_student <- tibble(id = 31, name = "Kalisa", district = "Huye")
bind_rows(students %>% select(id, name, district), new_student) %>% tail()
```

# tidyr: reshaping data

## pivot_longer(): wide to long

```{r pivot-longer}
long_data <- students %>%
  select(id, name, district, math, english, kinyarwanda) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = math:kinyarwanda,
               names_to = "subject", values_to = "score")
long_data
```

## pivot_wider(): long to wide

```{r pivot-wider}
long_data %>% pivot_wider(names_from = subject, values_from = score)

students %>%
  group_by(district, grade) %>%
  summarise(m = mean(math, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = grade, values_from = m)
```

## Missing values: drop_na(), replace_na()

```{r missing}
students %>% drop_na(math)
students %>% drop_na()
students %>% replace_na(list(math = 0, english = 0))
```

## unite() and separate()

```{r unite}
united <- students %>% unite("name_grade", name, grade, sep = "-")
united %>% select(name_grade)
united %>% separate(name_grade, into = c("name", "grade"), sep = "-")
```

## complete(): add missing combinations

```{r complete}
students %>%
  count(district, grade) %>%
  complete(district, grade, fill = list(n = 0))
```

# lubridate, stringr, forcats, purrr

```{r others}
# lubridate: dates
students %>%
  mutate(month = month(date, label = TRUE),
         year = year(date),
         week_no = week(date)) %>%
  count(month)

# stringr: text
students %>% filter(str_detect(name, "^U"))   # names starting with U
students %>% mutate(name_length = str_length(name)) %>% select(name, name_length)

# forcats: factors
students %>%
  mutate(district = fct_reorder(district, average)) %>%
  pull(district) %>%
  levels()

# purrr: apply a function over columns
students %>% select(math:kinyarwanda) %>% map_dbl(~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))
```

# ggplot2: charts

## Scatter plot

```{r scatter}
ggplot(students, aes(math, kinyarwanda, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Math vs Kinyarwanda", x = "Math", y = "Kinyarwanda") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Bar chart (counts)

```{r bar-counts}
ggplot(students, aes(district, fill = sex)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Students per district", x = NULL, y = "Count")
```

## Bar chart (values) + coord_flip

```{r bar-values}
students %>%
  group_by(district) %>%
  summarise(avg = mean(average)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(fct_reorder(district, avg), avg)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Average score")
```

## Boxplot

```{r boxplot}
ggplot(students, aes(grade, average, fill = grade)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_classic()
```

## Histogram and density

```{r hist-density}
ggplot(students, aes(average)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 10, fill = "tomato", color = "white")

ggplot(students, aes(average, fill = sex)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5)
```



## Facets: one panel per group

```{r facets}
ggplot(students, aes(math, english)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ district)
```

## Heatmap

```{r heatmap}
students %>%
  group_by(district, grade) %>%
  summarise(avg = mean(average), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(grade, district, fill = avg)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(avg, 1)), color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c()
```

## Scores by subject (long data)

```{r subject-box}
ggplot(long_data, aes(subject, score, fill = subject)) +
  geom_boxplot(na.rm = TRUE) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Save a plot

```{r ggsave, eval=FALSE}
# eval = FALSE: change to TRUE if you want to save the file when knitting
ggsave("plot.png", width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

# Full pipeline: dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2

```{r pipeline}
students %>%
  pivot_longer(math:kinyarwanda, names_to = "subject", values_to = "score") %>%
  drop_na(score) %>%
  group_by(grade, subject) %>%
  summarise(avg = mean(score), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(grade, avg, fill = subject)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Average score by grade and subject",
       x = "Grade", y = "Average", fill = "Subject") +
  theme_minimal()
```


##Conditional statements
Conditional statements allow R to make decisions based on student information.
## A. if statement

if (students$math[1] >= 50) {
  print("PASS")
} else {
  print("FAIL")
}
